# PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Aabenraa)

PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Aabenraa) is a Danish outpatient psychiatric unit that appears in the ADHD-databasen (ADHD database) 2024 report as one of the units measured against national quality indicators for ADHD treatment. The unit is notable primarily for a stark quality gap on one metric: it achieved only 18 percent fulfillment of Indicator 10, far below the 90 percent development target set for this measure [^src1].

Indicator 10 measures the share of adult treatment courses in which a patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of starting treatment. This was the first time the indicator had been reported nationally, and the results showed substantial shortfalls in meeting the 90 percent quality goal both nationally (37 percent) and regionally (14–52 percent). The steering group behind the ADHD database discussed the reasons for the low fulfillment rate, including registration practices and the underlying data from child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and decided to work on improving registration practice going forward. PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Aabenraa)'s result of 18 percent (with a confidence interval of 12–27) places it at the low end of this national picture, out of 115 relevant cases with 21 meeting the criterion [^src1].

The same report also credits PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Aabenraa) with a markedly higher score on a different metric — 94 out of 115 cases, or 82 percent (confidence interval 73–88) — recorded in the section of the report covering pages 56 to 60, which deals with Indicator 11, measuring whether adult patients were in ADHD medication treatment within 120 days of starting a package course of treatment. This indicator was also reported for the first time for adults in 2024, following the expansion of the ADHD database that year to include adult patients. National results for Indicator 11 showed wide regional variation, for instance Region Nordjylland at 85 percent versus Region Hovedstaden at 37 percent, a gap the report attributes probably to differences in registration practice rather than real clinical differences [^src2].

No relationships or additional claims involving PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Aabenraa) beyond these two indicator results are present in the available data.
